title: PhD in Germany Without IELTS 2027: Where the Certificate Is Actually Required
seoTitle: PhD in Germany Without IELTS 2027: Routes, Rules & Reality
seoDescription: Can you do a PhD in Germany without IELTS? Yes — on some routes. Where German universities ask for the certificate, where they don’t, and how to apply either way.
intro: German PhD admission is decentralised — so the IELTS rule depends on the route. Where the certificate is required, where it is not, and how to use both facts.
description: Where German universities require IELTS for PhD admission, where they do not, and how to apply without the certificate.
author: NextApply Team
excerpt: Where German universities require IELTS for PhD admission — and where you can genuinely skip the certificate.
content:
Germany is the easiest country in Europe to start a PhD without an IELTS certificate — not because its universities are lax, but because its doctoral admission is decentralised. There is no university-wide admissions office stamping every PhD file. You apply to a professor, a research group, or a structured programme, and each sets its own evidence rules. That decentralisation creates genuine, verifiable routes into German doctoral research without ever sitting IELTS — alongside routes where the certificate is non-negotiable. Knowing which is which is the whole game.

Why there is no single IELTS rule

German doctorates come in two shapes, and the English requirement follows the shape. In the traditional, still-dominant individual doctorate, a professor hires you the way a lab anywhere hires a researcher: your CV, publications, references and a conversation. When the working language is English — true across most STEM groups — the interview itself demonstrates your English better than any certificate, and many chairs simply never ask for one. In structured programmes — Max Planck International Research Schools (IMPRS), DFG Research Training Groups, graduate schools — a central office manages admissions, and its rules are written down: some require IELTS 6.5, many state that English tests are recommended but optional and judge language in the interview instead.

RouteHow admission worksIELTS reality
Individual doctorate (supervisor-based)You find a professor who agrees to supervise; often registered as an employed research associate (TV-L E13) or scholarship holder.Often no certificate demanded — the interview is the test. Some chairs still ask for IELTS/TOEFL evidence at HR stage.
Structured programme (IMPRS, graduate schools)Apply to a cohort with set deadlines, rotations and coursework.Mixed: many IMPRS state IELTS/TOEFL are "recommended, not required" and assess English in the interview; a few set hard floors.
DAAD-funded programmes (e.g. EPOS)Apply to a development-related master’s or PhD course with DAAD scholarship attached.Certificate usually required by the course itself — DAAD minimums apply. Plan for IELTS 6.0-6.5.

What replaces IELTS in practice

  • The interview. For employed positions — and a German PhD position is a job, paying TV-L E13 salaries around €4,500-5,300 gross per month — a 40-minute technical conversation in English is the real language test. A strong performance closes the question.
  • A Medium of Instruction letter. If your previous degree was taught in English, attach the MOI letter to your application proactively; most supervisors treat it as sufficient.
  • An English-taught master’s degree. A degree completed in English (in Germany, or anywhere) is accepted by nearly every structured programme as an exemption — check the call’s exact wording.
  • Writing you can show. A solid publication, thesis or preprint in English does more for a supervisor’s confidence than a band score, because it is the skill the doctorate actually uses.

Where the certificate is genuinely required

Three situations still demand a plan. Humanities and social-science doctorates taught in German expect German certificates (TestDaF, DSH) — a different problem, not an IELTS one. DAAD scholarship programmes, including EPOS development-related courses, carry the language requirements of the degree course itself, typically IELTS 6.0-6.5. And a minority of structured programmes publish hard IELTS floors — if the call says "required", treat it as required; in our audit of live German listings, the positions with no English-certificate requirement at all state it plainly, and each such card below is verified against its official page.

[[chart:e13-pay]]

Visa-wise, the German student visa for doctoral candidates does not impose a national English test; the block-account and university admission documents matter more — our blocked account guide covers the financial side.

Reading the ad’s language line

German job-style PhD advertisements use a handful of phrases, and each one means something specific. "Very good English skills" with no certificate mentioned is the permissive default — the interview decides. "Fluent English (C1)" frequently signals a structured programme that will accept evidence at its discretion; ask what evidence they accept before paying for a test. "IELTS/TOEFL required" or a CEFR level named alongside "proof" means what it says. Our cards preserve this wording verbatim so you can filter without opening fifty PDFs — and the positions listed below were checked line by line during our verification pass.

Daily life is the last piece. Leipzig, Heidelberg or Dresden function fine in English inside the lab, but registration offices (Bürgeramt), flat viewings and health-insurance paperwork mostly do not. A free Goethe A1 course before arrival — or in your first semester — removes friction no certificate requirement ever captures.

How to run the no-IELTS route

  • Target employed positions in STEM. Filter our German listings, read each ad’s language line, and prioritise those that mention no certificate — then email the group leader directly with a two-paragraph application, per our supervisor email templates.
  • Read structured-programme FAQs, not the homepage. IMPRS FAQ pages often state "IELTS/TOEFL recommended but not required" — exactly the wording you want, in writing.
  • Keep one test in reserve. If two target programmes hard-require IELTS, one Academic sitting (6.5) unlocks them while you continue the no-certificate route in parallel — both tracks can run at once.

The broader context — tuition-free study, stipends and salary schemes — is in our Germany guide, and the pay structure is explained in TV-L E13 explained. The live German positions below are all in our database with verified language requirements — several confirm in writing that no English certificate is needed at application.
